policy: Deceased person entities are pinned to their most publicly recognizable commemorative site, never a raw residence: (1) formally designated historic property (NHL/NRHP/city landmark), (2) institution formally dedicated to or holding the person's legacy, (3) publicly documented gravesite. Living persons: institution only, never a residence, explicit owner review required before any pin. Every pin carries a T1-T3-cited claim; every citation URL was opened and verified by the operator session on 2026-07-28 before inclusion. Coordinates are institution-precision (geohash 5), matching existing release pins (see ent_ida_b_wells_001).

records.locationLabel: Pauli Murray Family Home, 906 Carroll Street, Durham
records.designation: National Historic Landmark, designated December 23, 2016 (NPS); operates as the Pauli Murray Center for History and Social Justice
records.coordinateSource: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Pauli_Murray_Family_Home (DMS infobox, cross-checked against 906 Carroll Street address)

claim.object: The Pauli Murray Family Home at 906 Carroll Street in Durham, North Carolina, where Pauli Murray was raised by her grandparents and aunts from 1914 to 1948, was designated a National Historic Landmark in 2016 and now houses the Pauli Murray Center for History and Social Justice
claim.citationLabel: National Park Service: Pauli Murray Family Home

records.locationLabel: NASA Glenn Research Center, 21000 Brookpark Road, Cleveland
records.designation: Career site 1955-1989; no NHL/NRHP property or named facility for Easley exists, so her 34-year workplace is the best-documented public site

claim.object: Annie Easley worked as a human computer, mathematician, and computer programmer at NASA's Lewis Research Center, now Glenn Research Center, in Cleveland, Ohio, across a 34-year career from 1955 to her retirement in 1989
claim.citationLabel: NASA History: Annie Easley, Computer Scientist

records.siteName: the bell hooks center, Berea College
records.locationLabel: the bell hooks center, Draper Hall, Berea College, Berea, Kentucky
records.designation: Institutional center named for bell hooks at Berea College, where she taught as Distinguished Professor in Residence from 2004 and whose archives hold her papers; no NHL/NRHP property is associated with her
records.coordinateSource: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Berea_College (campus infobox, cross-checked against 101 Chestnut St address)

claim.object: bell hooks joined Berea College in Berea, Kentucky as Distinguished Professor in Residence in 2004, left her papers to its Special Collections and Archives, and is honored on campus by the bell hooks center in Draper Hall, an institutional center bearing her name
claim.citationLabel: Berea College: the bell hooks center

records.siteName: Alice Ball Memorial Chaulmoogra Tree, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa
records.locationLabel: Alice Ball Memorial Chaulmoogra Tree, Bachman Hall, University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa, Honolulu
records.designation: Commemorative chaulmoogra tree planted in her honor by King Prajadhipok of Siam in 1935, with dedicatory plaque installed circa 2000, on the campus where she developed the Ball Method; no NHL/NRHP property is associated with her
records.coordinateSource: Bachman Hall, 2444 Dole Street geocode, cross-checked against UH Mānoa campus coordinates on Wikipedia

claim.object: Alice Ball is memorialized on the University of Hawaiʻi at Mānoa campus by a chaulmoogra tree gifted and planted in her honor by King Prajadhipok of Siam in 1935 near Bachman Hall, with a dedicatory plaque installed circa 2000, at the institution where she developed the Ball Method
claim.citationLabel: UH Mānoa Campus Arboretum: Chaulmoogra Tree

records.locationLabel: Audre Lorde Residence, 207 St. Paul's Avenue, Staten Island
records.designation: New York City Individual Landmark LP-2642, designated June 18, 2019 by the NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission; verified not NRHP/NHL-listed
records.coordinateSource: NYC Open Data Individual Landmark Sites dataset (LPC parcel centroid, Block 516 Lot 32)

claim.object: 207 St. Paul's Avenue in Staten Island was the primary residence of Audre Lorde from 1972 to 1987, where she wrote some of her most ground-breaking work; the New York City Landmarks Preservation Commission designated it an Individual Landmark in June 2019
claim.citationLabel: NYC Landmarks Preservation Commission: Audre Lorde Residence Designation Report (LP-2642)

records.locationLabel: James Baldwin Residence, 137 West 71st Street, New York
records.designation: Listed on the National Register of Historic Places September 3, 2019 (Ref. 100004332); also a New York City Individual Landmark (LP-2636, June 18, 2019)
records.coordinateSource: https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/National_Register_of_Historic_Places_listings_in_Manhattan_from_59th_to_110th_Streets (NRHP list entry, cross-checked against same-block Dorilton Apartments coordinates)

claim.object: James Baldwin resided at 137 West 71st Street in Manhattan from 1965 until his death in 1987, the building that served as his primary American residence; it was designated a New York City Individual Landmark and entered in the National Register of Historic Places in 2019 for its association with him

records.locationLabel: Lorraine Hansberry House, 6140 S. Rhodes Avenue, Chicago
records.designation: Chicago Landmark, designated February 10, 2010 by the Chicago City Council (Landmark ID L-291); the house at the center of Hansberry v. Lee (1940). Note: her NYC residence at 337 Bleecker Street is separately NRHP-listed (2021, Ref. 100006490) but has a narrower public profile
records.coordinateSource: City of Chicago Individual Landmarks open-data record L-291 (lat 41.78273878850, lng -87.61242010460), cross-checked against the Chicago Landmarks commission detail page address

claim.object: The Hansberry family home at 6140 S. Rhodes Avenue in Chicago, purchased by Carl Hansberry in 1937 in defiance of a racially restrictive covenant and defended through the U.S. Supreme Court case Hansberry v. Lee, inspired Lorraine Hansberry's A Raisin in the Sun; the Chicago City Council designated it a Chicago Landmark on February 10, 2010
claim.citationLabel: Commission on Chicago Landmarks: Lorraine Hansberry House
